Definition: to open wide (literally or figuratively); specifically, to loosen, begin, plough, carve
BiblicalUsage: Pathach means to open wide, to open, to loosen, to begin. The windows of heaven are opened in the flood in Genesis 7:11, and Samuel opens the doors of the house of the Lord in 1 Samuel 3:15. The psalmist prays in Psalm 51:15, O Lord, open thou my lips, and my mouth shall show forth thy praise, and in Psalm 118:19, open to me the gates of righteousness. Isaiah 22:22 promises the key of David: he shall open, and none shall shut.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe opening is God's work before it is ours: He opens the heavens, the doors, the lips, and the gates, and the key of David opens what no man can shut. My position is that the prayer to open my lips is the prayer I should pray first, because praise begins where He opens.
